overview: Liechtenstein is a tiny landlocked country in the Alps, between Switzerland and Austria. Its capital is Vaduz. Liechtenstein is a principality, ruled by a prince, and it uses the Swiss franc as its currency. It has had no army since the 1860s. Despite its small size, it has one of the highest incomes per person in the world.

geography.text: Liechtenstein is one of only two doubly landlocked countries in the world: it is surrounded only by other landlocked countries. Its western part lies in the flat valley of the Rhine, which forms the border with Switzerland, while the east rises steeply into the Alps.

history.text: The princely family of Liechtenstein bought the lands of Schellenberg and Vaduz around 1700, and in 1719 the Holy Roman Emperor made them a principality. Liechtenstein became fully sovereign in 1806. It abolished its army in 1868 and has been closely tied to Switzerland since forming a customs union with it in 1923.

events.title: Principality created
events.text: The lands are raised to a principality named after the Liechtenstein family.

events.title: Sovereignty
events.text: Liechtenstein becomes a sovereign state as the Holy Roman Empire collapses.

events.title: Army abolished
events.text: Liechtenstein gets rid of its army.

events.title: Customs union with Switzerland
events.text: Liechtenstein ties its economy to Switzerland.

events.title: Joins the UN
events.text: Liechtenstein becomes a member of the United Nations.

government.text: Liechtenstein is a constitutional monarchy. The Prince has more power than most European monarchs: he can veto laws and dismiss the government. The people also have strong powers through referendums. The Landtag, its 25-member parliament, is elected every four years.

economy.text: Liechtenstein is one of the richest countries in the world per person. Despite its small size, it has a strong high-tech industry, including the world's leading maker of false teeth, and a big financial sector. It uses the Swiss franc, and more people commute in to work each day than live there.

culture.text: Liechtenstein is a German-speaking country of castles and mountain villages. Vaduz Castle, home of the princely family, overlooks the capital. The Prince's art collection, one of the finest private collections in the world, is shown partly in Vienna.

items.title: Vaduz Castle
items.text: The prince's home, high above the capital.

items.title: Postage stamps
items.text: Liechtenstein's stamps are famous among collectors.

sport.text: Skiing is Liechtenstein's most successful sport. Hanni Wenzel won two Olympic gold medals in 1980, and the country has won more Winter Olympic medals per person than any other nation.

items.title: Hanni Wenzel
items.text: Won two Olympic golds and a silver in 1980.

items.title: Winter Olympics
items.text: Ten medals for a country of about 40,000 people.

didYouKnow: Liechtenstein is one of only two countries in the world that are doubly landlocked.
Liechtenstein is one of the world's biggest makers of false teeth.
